name: How to Prepare for an In-Law Suite Design-Build Consultation

step.name: Step 1: Define the Suite’s Intended Use
step.text: List the people who may use the space, whether occupancy will be occasional or full time, and what independence is expected. Decide whether the suite needs only a bedroom and bathroom or a complete living area with cooking, laundry, and a separate entrance. Write down mobility, hearing, vision, or privacy considerations before meeting a contractor. Done means you can describe the occupant’s daily routine and identify features that cannot be compromised.

step.name: Step 2: Compare the Available Locations
step.text: Evaluate an existing bedroom, a garage, a side-yard addition, an upper-level area, or a detached structure. Check access from the street, distance to the main home, natural light, ceiling conditions, available storage, and whether the proposed location affects parking or outdoor space. A garage conversion may reduce construction in some areas but can require substantial work to make the space suitable for living. Do not assume that an enclosed garage is already ready for residential occupancy.

step.name: Step 3: Gather Property Information
step.text: Have the property address, existing floor plans if available, site measurements, photographs, utility locations, prior remodeling records, and any known drainage or foundation concerns ready. Note the service panel location, water-heater location, sewer or septic arrangement, and paths that could support new plumbing. The approving agency may differ between a city property and an unincorporated county property. County materials also identify additional considerations for ADUs served by private wells or onsite wastewater systems, so disclose those conditions early.

step.name: Step 4: Confirm the Approval Path
step.text: Ask the design-build provider which project category best fits the concept and what local agency should review it. A private bedroom and bathroom connected to the home may have different requirements from an independent ADU with its own kitchen and entrance. Ask what drawings, energy information, structural details, inspections, and occupancy documentation may be required. Do not order materials or begin demolition until the project’s approval path and construction scope are clear.

step.name: Step 5: Develop the Layout and Accessibility Plan
step.text: Place the bedroom, bathroom, living area, storage, and entrance around the occupant’s routine rather than fitting fixtures into leftover space. Consider step-free access, door clearances, lighting, bathroom maneuvering space, ventilation, privacy from shared areas, and emergency egress. Elite Remodeling & Design describes using design development and, depending on scope, 3D visualization to help clients review proposed spaces before construction. Use the design review to identify awkward door swings, insufficient storage, poor furniture placement, or difficult transitions.

step.name: Step 6: Request a Detailed Design-Build Proposal
step.text: Ask for a written scope covering design, demolition, structural work, framing, insulation, windows, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, cabinets, countertops, tile, fixtures, painting, site work, permitting coordination, inspections, and final completion tasks. Confirm which selections are included and how allowances or changes will be handled. Compare proposals line by line instead of relying only on the total. The best fit is the proposal that clearly matches the intended use, existing conditions, responsibilities, and desired finish level.

step.name: Step 7: Confirm the Preconstruction Plan
step.text: Before work begins, review the final drawings, selections, contract scope, payment schedule, access arrangements, dust control, material storage, and communication process. Confirm where the occupant will live during disruptive work and which utilities may be temporarily unavailable. Done means the household understands the sequence and the provider has the information needed to begin. Contact Elite Remodeling & Design with the property details and suite goals to start a project discussion.
